body:
Thursday, October 22, 2026 74° Today's Paper
Honolulu firefighters extinguished a residential high-rise building fire this afternoon on South King Street.
The Honolulu Fire Department received a 911 call at 3:08 p.m. today for a fire at 1239 South King St., and sent six units staffed with 22 personnel, according to a news release. Google Maps identifies the building as Wisteria Vista.
The first unit arrived five minutes later to find an eight-story building with no visible smoke or flames. Firefighters discovered fire on the seventh floor and began attacking the fire.
Two residents, a man and a woman in their 60s, were extricated and transferred to the care of Honolulu Emergency Medical Services.
The fire was deemed under control and extinguished at 3:38 p.m.
An investigation is underway to determine the fire’s origin, cause and damage estimates.

Sprinkler extinguishes fire in Madison apartment on Thursday
body:
MADISON, Wis. (WMTV) - A fire in a Madison apartment was extinguished Thursday night due to an automated sprinkler, the Madison Fire Department announced Friday.
According to the department, firefighters went to an apartment complex at 6834 Milwaukee Street just after 8:30 p.m. after the people that lived there thought a pipe had busted.
Upon arrival, firefighters found alarms sounding and people had evacuated the apartment.
Firefighters found smoke in the hallway and shut off an active fire sprinkler in the utility room, officials said.
Firefighters found a charred cardboard box with cigarette butts. The improperly discarded smoking materials were determined to be the ignition source, the department explained.
The sprinkler activation impacted a person in the apartment unit below, and three people were displaced from two apartments, officials explained.
The department said the fire was controlled and extinguished by one sprinkler head, marking the second time a sprinkler stopped a fire in an apartment this week.
On Sept. 5, a cart outside the trash room of a student high rise caught fire and a sprinkler activation occurred.
“This call demonstrates the effectiveness of automatic fire sprinklers in containing, controlling, and sometimes extinguishing fire,” Madison Fire said. “When a residence is not protected by automatic fire sprinklers, fire has time to grow in size and severity before firefighters arrive, impacting several households and possibly leading to injury or fatality to occupants and firefighters. The Madison Fire Department strongly encourages the installation of fire protection systems in all commercial and residential properties.”
Fire damage was contained to the cardboard box and miscellaneous contents within the box.

Vienna Fire Department Rescues Several People from Burning Residential Building
body:
In the night of Sunday, August 29, 2026, a large apartment fire occurred in a multi-family house on Schüttelstraße in the 2nd district. Several residents had to be rescued by the Vienna professional fire brigade.
Upon the arrival of the emergency services, an apartment on the 3rd floor was in flames. Flames were shooting out of a courtyard-facing window, while the stairwell was heavily smoked from the fire floor upwards.
The resident of the apartment on fire was able to get to safety in time. Other residents of the building made themselves noticeable at the windows or fled to their balconies, according to the fire department.
The fire brigade immediately initiated a comprehensive firefighting attack. A breathing apparatus team laid a hose line through the stairwell into the apartment on fire. At the same time, extinguishing was carried out from the outside to prevent the flames from spreading to the apartment above.
Additional breathing apparatus teams checked the stairwell and adjacent apartments.
During this, an injured person was found in the stairwell and brought outside. Two more people were rescued via a turntable ladder. A fourth person was brought to safety with an escape filter mask through the smoky stairwell.
In total, the fire department handed over nine people to the special operations group of the Vienna professional rescue service. Four people had to be taken to a hospital.
During the firefighting operations, the emergency services also removed a medical oxygen tank from the fire apartment.
High-performance ventilation devices were used to ventilate and air out the building. According to the professional fire department, the fire could be extinguished quickly due to these measures.
After about two hours, the operation was completed. The fire department was on site with 41 emergency personnel and nine vehicles.

Five missing , eight injured after fire destroys building in Swiss town
body:
Five people are missing, and eight others have been injured after a fire destroyed a restaurant and apartments in the Swiss Alpine town of Thusis.
The blaze broke out shortly after midnight local time on Friday, with initial investigations indicating that the fire started on the second floor of the building.
Nearly 100 firefighters were called to the scene in the eastern Swiss town, according to Graubünden cantonal police. The building was described as being “completely destroyed” by the fire.
The intensity of the blaze caused the stairwell to collapse, forcing firefighters to use a crane to open the roof as they worked to control the flames.
Fourteen people managed to escape the building. Police said two of those rescued were seriously injured, while two suffered moderate injuries and four sustained minor injuries.
The injured were taken to hospitals in nearby Chur, Thusis, Ilanz and Zurich for treatment.
However, five people remain unaccounted for, with emergency services continuing efforts to establish their whereabouts.

Thusis is located in the canton of Graubünden, an Alpine region known for its mountain scenery and popularity with tourists throughout the year. The area attracts visitors for winter sports as well as hiking and other outdoor activities during the warmer months.
Authorities have urged people to avoid the affected area while emergency and investigative operations continue.

Woman gets jail for setting fire to Sembawang flat , had believed she was trapped in ex - boyfriend house
body:
A woman who set fire to papers in a Sembawang HDB flat after believing she was trapped inside has been sentenced to five months' jail on Wednesday (Sept 9).
Jasmine Helena Halim, 46, admitted to one charge of intentionally setting fire to the unit.
The fire broke out at around 5.15pm on June 30 at a 10th-floor unit at Block 512 Wellington Circle.
Jasmine had broken up with her boyfriend on the day of the fire and, at around 5pm, became convinced that he had trapped her inside her home, reported Shin Min Daily News.
She reportedly told an investigation officer that she had been locked inside the unit for weeks without food, although she had not sought help from anyone during that time, Shin Min reported.
She then used a lighter to set fire to six pieces of paper and threw them into the bedroom in an alleged attempt to create an "escape route", causing the flames to quickly spread and damage her home and the windows of a neighbouring unit.
SCDF officers later extinguished the blaze and evacuated about 30 residents.

Chicago Fire Union Raises Concerns Over Single - Stairwell Buildings
body:
The president of the Chicago firefighters union says safety is a major concern in the single-stairwell buildings. They prefer two exit stairways, making it easier for residents to escape a fire while firefighters have space to do their work.
A group of advocates is pushing for a change in Chicago’s building code that they say will kick off development and create badly needed housing.
They want to pass an ordinance allowing developers to construct a single staircase for residential buildings of up to five stories, instead of the required two staircases.
That would make the construction of small apartment or condo buildings less expensive, helping developers fill Chicago’s empty lots with units that are also affordable, said Ald. Matt Martin, 47th, who introduced the ordinance in 2025.
“Our goal is to build more affordable housing,” Martin said. “We don’t see a lot of three- to four-story buildings going up, and we’re also losing a lot of family-sized units.”
The proposal has drawn criticism from Chicago firefighters, who say new single-staircase buildings wouldn’t meet the city’s safety standards. They prefer two exit stairways, making it easier for residents to escape a fire. The current building code typically allows a single staircase for residential buildings with three stories or less. Fire escapes don’t count as exit stairways under the building code.
The controversy is unlikely to end soon. Housing advocates say rising rents and the slow pace of housing construction make it necessary to find new ways to build. They expect the City Council will vote on the issue in the coming months, perhaps after the February mayoral election.
But many firefighters seem equally determined to preserve Chicago’s two-staircase rule.

Indian students from Keralam killed in Germany building fire
BERLIN: Three Indian students from Keralam were killed and five other people injured after a fire broke out at a residential building in Bochum, Germany, early on October 13, Tuesday. German authorities have provisionally arrested a 41-year-old Romanian national who lived in the same building on suspicion of murder, as investigators probe whether the blaze was deliberately set. The Indian Embassy in Berlin has confirmed the deaths and said that it is coordinating with local authorities to assist the affected families.

In a post on X on October 13, Wednesday, the embassy expressed its condolences to the families and confirmed that the incident was under investigation by German authorities. “Three Indian nationals (two women and one man) have tragically lost their lives in a fire incident in Bochum, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Fire crews race to blaze in Bristol tower block
body:
Fire appliances attending an incident at Spencer House in Redcliffe, Bristol, on Sunday evening, August 16(Image: Bristol Post submitted)
Emergency services from across Bristol rushed to a large tower block near the city centre this evening, to reports of a fire.
Fire crews from several fire stations, along with police, attended and found a fire in the bin chute at Spencer House in Redcliffe.
A large number of fire appliances attended as is policy when it comes to fires involving Bristol's tall buildings, but thankfully, the fire was quickly under control and extinguished with no injuries and no need to evacuate the residents.
Spencer House is one of Bristol's largest tower blocks, stretching from Clarence Road alongside the New Cut River Avon to Somerset Square, with 88 flats in its 11 storeys.
A spokesperson for Avon Fire and Rescue Service said: "We were able to extinguish the fire reasonably quickly, and then made sure the smoke cleared from the building using natural ventilation - basically we opened all the windows in the areas affected.
"We are recording this as deliberate ignition - someone has thrown something on fire down the chute from an upper floor and it has set everything else in there on fire," he added.
"We will be passing that over to Bristol City Council, which manages the block, and they will have their own procedures to go through now to ascertain who has done this and what action can be taken," he added.
The fire came as Avon Fire and Rescue Service - along with fire services across the West Country - are dealing with a high number of call-outs to attend wildfires and grassfires on open spaces around the West of England, as fire is easily spreading on the tinder-dry land.
